assessments.reasoning: The pinned inheritance chapter puts a single-class upper bound on the direct parents of a class or object while permitting several interface parents. It also identifies the default superclass when the declaration omits one.

challenge.method: Check whether multiple interface parents or the prohibition on inheriting from an object undermines the rule for an object type.
challenge.results: Interface parents are counted separately. The prohibition concerns using an object as a parent, whereas the claim concerns the parents an object may have. The special root and backend behavior are outside scope.

limitations: Interface types follow a distinct rule. The special root type and individual backend implementations are outside this claim.
Pinned Kotlin/Core rule for class and object types, with the special root and platform-specific implementations outside the stated scope.
